title: Friendships: Choose What Happens Next
summary: Three situations about someone being picked on, a rumour, and being left out. The teen chooses, sees what might happen, and the psychologist leads the discussion.
clinicianNotes: Original scenarios and conversation starters. They are not a measure of mental health. Draft content: needs review by a licensed psychologist and a cultural fit check before use with patients.

scenarios.title: In the canteen
scenarios.story: Some older students keep mocking a younger boy for how he talks. People are watching and nobody is saying anything.

options.text: Sit down next to him, talk about something else, and tell a teacher afterwards.
options.outcome: The mocking stops. He gives a small smile, and you feel proud you did something.
options.note: Shows support and uses adult help. Explore the courage this took and what helped.

options.outcome: It ends on its own, but you keep thinking about the boy's face.
options.note: Bystander silence is common. Explore fear of becoming a target.

options.text: Laugh along so they do not pick on you.
options.outcome: The group laughs harder, and you feel uncomfortable afterwards.
options.note: Laughing often protects belonging. Explore the pressure the teen felt.

scenarios.keyMessage: Small acts of kindness stop bullying. You do not have to be loud to help.
scenarios.discussion: What is one small thing you could do if you saw someone being picked on?

scenarios.title: The rumour
scenarios.story: You find out a friend has been spreading a rumour about you. Your face goes hot and your hands shake.

options.text: Calm down first, then ask the friend privately what happened and say how it made you feel.
options.outcome: Your friend looks ashamed and says sorry. You both feel relieved.
options.note: Pauses before acting and uses a private, honest talk. Explore how the teen calmed down.

options.text: Say nothing, but stop talking to them.
options.outcome: The silence feels cold and the friendship fades without any answers.
options.note: Withdrawal avoids a fight but leaves hurt unspoken. Explore what the teen fears might happen if they spoke up.

options.text: Spread a rumour about them back.
options.outcome: The conflict grows and more people get involved and hurt.
options.note: Retaliation often follows hurt. Explore what the teen really wanted from the friend.

scenarios.keyMessage: Pausing before you react gives you choices. A private, honest talk can fix more than revenge.
scenarios.discussion: What helps you calm down when you feel hurt or angry?

scenarios.title: The weekend plan
scenarios.story: Your group of friends made a weekend plan without telling you. You find out when you see the photos.

options.text: Tell one friend you felt hurt and ask what happened, and make your own plan with someone else.
options.outcome: The friend says it was a mix-up and invites you next time. You feel less alone.
options.note: Names the feeling and takes care of self. Explore whether this approach feels realistic.

options.text: Pretend you do not care and stay away from the group for a while.
options.outcome: You avoid the hurt, but you feel lonely and the distance grows.
options.note: Pretending protects pride but isolates. Explore what the teen is afraid of showing.

options.text: Post something angry about them online.
options.outcome: Everyone sees it, the situation gets worse, and trust drops.
options.note: Public anger often comes from hurt. Explore what the teen hoped would happen.

scenarios.keyMessage: Feeling left out hurts. Talking to one person you trust is a good first step.
scenarios.discussion: Who is one friend you could talk to when you feel left out?
